request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary

Patient: 35-year-old G2P2 female

Admission date: [insert date]
Discharge date: [insert date]
Admission diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital course:
The patient was admitted to the CCU on [insert date] with complaints of retrosternal chest discomfort radiating to jaw, associated with nausea and diaphoresis. Based on physical examination, EKG and cardiac enzyme levels, as well as coronary angiography and TTE results, the patient was diagnosed with an acute inferior STEMI secondary to spontaneous dissection of the OM2.

Treatment:
The patient was appropriately discharged on dual antiplatelet therapy including ASA and Clopidogrel including beta blockade with Metoprolol.

Follow-up plan:
The patient was advised to continue with the prescribed medication and instructed to come for follow-up after one month.

Readmission:
One month later, the patient returned with diplopia and numbness of her left arm and face. Computed tomographic angiography showed a focal 8mm long dissection of the right vertebral artery in its V1 segment with mild associated aneurysmal dilatation. The patient was subsequently started on anticoagulation therapy to prevent future spontaneous dissections.

Discharge condition:
The patient's condition was stable at the time of discharge.

Discharge disposition:
The patient was discharged home with family members.

Follow-up plan:
The patient was advised to continue with the prescribed medication and instructed to come for follow-up after three months.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
**CODE: I21**

The principal diagnosis is the acute inferior STEMI, established after ECG, cardiac enzymes, coronary angiography and TTE. The underlying cause, spontaneous dissection of the OM2 coronary branch, is recorded as an additional code and does not change the principal category. The later right vertebral artery dissection was found at readmission and belongs to a separate episode.
